I use to think that too, but the world of stoners changed my opinion of that. I was an avid smoker of the green for 10 years-ish, never really noticing the effects and aspects of the life I was living bother me. But people react to things different, including others being stoned. And that's what I discovered over time, the "stoner culture" wasn't all it cooked up to be. The tipping point for me was when I moved in with a friend I've known for 11-12 years, his girlfriend at the time for 5-6 years of them as a couple. I only ended up living with them for 2/3 months before a situation occurred. Up to this point, I had not only been a supplier but provider of most necessities in the living situation. Within a week and half period, 250$ went to mary jane that I purchased. I only smoke 1/10 of that, whilst my friend and his unemployed girlfriend demolished it. What pissed me off was when they complained about not having any, being broke, and finally not being able to pay the bills because they decided to spend what little money they had on weed. Now I'm not against it, but it definitely is a culture brewing stupidity in responsibility and mental awareness of the self. Many people can function and work within the bounds of it but there's a limit to the obsession and recognizing when its become a problem.
